newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: U.N. chief concerned over Angola peace deal delays.
newsitem.headline: U.N. chief concerned over Angola peace deal delays.

text.p: Secretary-General Boutros Boutros-Ghali expressed concern on Monday over ongoing delays in implementing a peace accord in Angola and recommended a U.N. operation there be extended for only two months.
The U.N. chief was particularly critical about former rebels of the National Union for the Total Independence of Angola (UNITA) in carrying out the accord.

"While the ceasefire is holding and the parties continue to profess their commitment to the Lusaka Protocol, the lack of significant progress in the peace process over the past three months is a source of serious concern," he said in a sharply worded report to the Security Council.
He was referring to an agreement signed in Lusaka, Zambia, in November 1994, ending nearly two decades of civil war between the Angolan government and UNITA.

"Nearly two years after the signing of the Protocol, the continuing delays and unfulfilled promises, particularly on the part of UNITA, in implementing the successive timetables for the completion of key military and political issues are no longer acceptable," Boutros-Ghali said.
He said the 7,264-member U.N. Angola Verificiation Mission III (UNAVEM III), was the largest U.N. peacekeeping operation. It costs more than $165 million for the six-month period ending December 31.

Unless serious progress was made in several key areas before the expiry of UNAVEM III's three-month mandate on October 11, "I recommend that the council consider only a short extension of the mandate, perhaps until December 11, so that it can keep the situation in Angola under close review and respond apporopriately to continuing delays, especially by UNITA," he added.

"At a time when funds for peacekeeping are scarcer than ever and all expenditures of the organisation are being closely scrutinised, it is becoming increasingly difficult to generate international support for operations which do not enjoy the full cooperation of the conflicting parties."

Boutros-Ghali said it was unfortunate UNITA leader Jonas Savimbi had failed to attend an October 2 meeting in Luanda of the Southern African Development Community (SADC), since that would have been a good opportunity for a meeting on Angolan soil with Angolan President Jose Eduardo dos Santos.
If UNITA felt Savimbi could not assume a vice-presidential post in a new government it should make a meaningful counter-proposal as soon as possible, he said.
Despite considerable delays, it should still be possible for UNAVEM III to fulfil most of its tasks by the originally envisaged completion date of February 8, 1997, the secretary-general said.

He therefore intended withdrawing some infantry and support units by the end of December, with further troop reductions to depend on progress made in carrying out the remaining provisions of the peace accord.
